text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finnish telecommunications group Nokia's mobile telephones breakthrough due more to luck and its rivals' errors than to planning, doctoral dissertation says.
- A half-kg pack of coffee could go up as high as 30 markka in August due to massive increases in raw coffee prices.
- No freeloaders allowed in the next round of pay talks -- agreement requires every sector's participation, Per-Erik Lundh, chairman of the Finnish Metal Workers' Union says.
- Finnish NATO membership is possible sometime in the future, Conservative Party's management says.
- EMU discussion between the government and opposition should begin soon, leaders of the Centre Party say.
- Law on equal retiring ages for men and women delayed due after Social and Health Ministry rejects model offered by labour market organisations.
- Experts believe biotech industry may be Finland's next international success story.
KAUPPALEHTI
- EMU membership would enhance competitiveness of small and middle sized companies, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says.
- Reports on natural gas potential should be finished and decision made by year-end: if not, nuclear could become an option again.
- Unofficial poll suggests 116 MPs support nuclear power if its use were linked to domestic wood processing, says Pekka Kuosmanen, Conservative -- promises parliament debate on issue.
- Finnish forestry companies selling thousands of blocks of holiday land.
- External pressure forces companies to change environmental attitudes, a doctoral dissertation says.
AAMULEHTI
- Government not planning new spending cuts to improve state economy, says Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto.
- The government should really ease income tax burden on low and middle income workers, says metal workers' Lundh.
- System of voluntary leave to create jobs to be made permanent next autumn: every 10th worker seems willing to join in, Labour Ministry study shows.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish Metal Workers' Union council will vote on their EMU stand on Tuesday, Leftist Alliance split on the question.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- ALKO managing director Ilkka Suominen could get backing from Germany, Carl Bildt, for nomination to the post of EU's special representative to Bosnia.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
